'''''Eriocapitella'' × ''hybrida''''' is a [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]] of [[flowering plant]] in the buttercup family [[Ranunculaceae]].{{r|POWO}} The parents of the hybrid are ''[[Eriocapitella japonica|E. japonica]]'' and ''[[Eriocapitella vitifolia|E. vitifolia]]''. Cultivars of the hybrid are commonly known as '''Japanese anemone hybrids'''.{{sfnp|Herman|2004}}

==Description==

''Eriocapitella'' × ''hybrida'' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]] up to {{cvt|1.5|m|ft|1}} tall. It forms large clumps of dark green, [[Glossary of leaf morphology#Leaf structure|ternate]], [[basal leaf|basal leaves]] on long [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]s (leaf stalks). The [[Trichome#Aerial surface hairs|pubescent]] leaflets are [[Glossary of botanical terms#ovate|ovate]], with deep lobes and [[Leaf#Margins (edge)|serrate]] margins (edges). The [[inflorescence]] is a large, loose [[Inflorescence#Determinate or cymose|cyme]] with semi-[[double flower]]s. The [[flower]] is approximately {{cvt|8|cm|in|1}} across with 7–11 white, pink, or rose [[sepal]]s (no [[petal]]s) each having a silky sheen on the backside. The center of the flower is surrounded by prominent golden [[stamen]]s.{{r|Anisko2008}}

==Taxonomy==

''Eriocapitella'' × ''hybrida'' was described by [[Maarten J. M. Christenhusz]] and [[James W. Byng]] in 2018.{{r|IPNI}} Like other members of genus ''Eriocapitella'', ''E.'' × ''hybrida'' was formerly a member of genus ''[[Anemone]]''. In particular, the historically important [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] ''Anemone'' × ''hybrida'' <small>Paxton</small> and the [[basionym]] ''Anemone japonica'' var. ''hybrida'' <small>L.H.Bailey</small> were described in 1848 and 1914, respectively.{{r|POWO:708423-1|Paxton1849|POWO:77187780-1|Bailey1919}}

==Ecology==

''Eriocapitella'' × ''hybrida'' along with four other [[taxa]] ([[Eriocapitella hupehensis|''E. hupehensis'']], ''[[Eriocapitella japonica|E. japonica]]'', [[Eriocapitella tomentosa|''E. tomentosa'']], and ''[[Eriocapitella vitifolia|E. vitifolia]]'') are known as '''fall-blooming anemones'''.{{sfnp|Rudy|2004}} The bloom period depends on the particular cultivar and location, but at [[Longwood Gardens]] for example, ''E.'' × ''hybrida'' 'Königin Charlotte' bloomed from mid September to early November.{{r|Anisko2008}}

==Cultivation==

The artificial hybrid ''Eriocapitella'' × ''hybrida'' was developed at the [[Royal Horticultural Society#Royal Horticultural Society gardens|gardens of the Royal Horticultural Society]] in 1848. As reported by [[Joseph Paxton]] at the time, gardeners crossed the so-called Japanese anemone [[Eriocapitella japonica|''E. japonica'']] with [[Eriocapitella vitifolia|''E. vitifolia'']] to produce a hardy fall-blooming hybrid with rose-colored flowers. The parent species were previously brought to England from their native Asia: ''E. vitifolia'' was brought from Nepal in 1829 while ''E. japonica'' was brought from China in 1844. European horticulturalists in Great Britain, Germany, and France subsequently introduced dozens of cultivars. Commonly called '''Japanese anemone hybrids''', the cultivars of ''E.'' × ''hybrida'' have single, semi-double, or [[double flower]]s with white, pink, or purple sepals.{{sfnp|Herman|2004}}{{r|Anisko2008|Paxton1849}}

At the [[Chicago Botanic Garden]], Rudy experimented with 26 [[cultivar]]s of fall-blooming anemones over a 5-year period beginning in 1998. His experiments included 18 cultivars of ''E.'' × ''hybrida'', of which more than half had a bloom length greater than 48 days.{{sfnp|Rudy|2004}}
